title: 📸Ari Espay #theatre #plays #janeausten #prideandprejudice #arethebenn...
transcript: this brand new adaptation of Pride and Prejudice updates the dialogue to feel like modern American speech including the vernacular the dialects the mannerisms of the characters the adaptation is called Are the Bennett girls Ok? and from the writing, to the direction, to the acting they're clearly trying to create this painfully familiar family/sibling dynamic especially in the way that they communicate the dialogue is free flowing and chaotic often overlapping often very barbed clearly trying to make it sound as organic to our ear as possible even to the point where it almost felt improvised and underneath these interactions there's this deep sense of intimacy intermingled with all of the tension overall I found it really funny and entertaining although the question did cross my mind of like do you need to update Jane Austen's dialogue to create this effect? now I have to confess that I've actually never read the book and I don't remember the 2005 movie that well there's at least one extremely obvious and actually quite audacious change to the plot that they make right at the end but otherwise I'm not sure what else was changed or reinterpreted aside from the dialogue but Jane Austen clearly still resonates with people very strongly to this day so it's worth asking like what the modernization and Americanization brings to the table especially if they're keeping the period setting again? I'm obviously not the best person to say but my gut feeling just in how I perceived the play is that there's just inevitably something different about watching actors deliver dialogue that is SO in their own voices almost in their bones like they've tapped into just a different kind of raw immediacy especially in the sense of humor I think my one issue with the play is that sometimes it felt like they were so focused on establishing these relationship dynamics and almost riffing around with a dialogue sometimes at the expense of telling the overarching story in a focused and coherent way still though, overall it definitely worked for me I was very entertained by this so Bedlam Theatre's production of are the Bennett girls ok? was just extended through November 9th at the West End Theatre
